newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl aide says could meet SPD in April on taxes.
newsitem.headline: Kohl aide says could meet SPD in April on taxes.

text.p: A senior aide to German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Wednesday that talks with the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on the government's tax reform could begin at the end of April.
Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl said the government must first prepare a draft tax reform bill before it could begin talks with the federal states, the SPD and others as Kohl has proposed.
"We will have the bill finished in April and then we can begin talks immediately, that means around three or four weeks after Easter," he told east German InfoRadio.
The SPD wants Bonn to bring forward its plan to cut income tax rates to 1998 from 1999 and to scrap plans to finance part of the reform by raising value added taxes (VAT).
Bohl said the government would first decide on the basic income tax rates before making any decisions on indirect taxes.
He added that the government still hoped cuts in corporate taxes could take effect next year as planned.
